task.text: Spawning a `Unit` from a prototype changes the prototype too.
`Unit.copy()` builds a new `Unit`, but the new unit and the old one still share state. A grunt that learns `rage` teaches it to every orc ever spawned.

items: A copy has the same name, hp and abilities as its source, and shares no mutable state with it, in either direction.
A `Unit` never keeps the list its caller passed to the constructor.
Keep the `Prototype<Unit>` contract, `Unit.copy()` returning `Unit`, and `Barracks.spawn(kind)` returning a fresh copy.

checks.title: A copy carries the same state
Teaching the copy leaves the original alone
Teaching the original leaves the copy alone
The constructor copies its input list
No mutable field is shared by a copy

hints.text: A copy that reuses the same `List` object is a shallow copy: two references, one list. Ask which fields are mutable objects rather than values.
Give every `Unit` its own `ArrayList`. Do it in the constructor, so it covers both `copy()` and callers that pass in a list they keep using.
